onboarding.preset.gemini.step1: Sign in to Google AI Studio with a Google account. It is not available everywhere; for example, it cannot be reached directly from mainland China or Hong Kong.
onboarding.preset.gemini.step2: On the “Get API key” page, choose “Create API key”, copy the key and paste it below.
onboarding.preset.gemini.step3: The free tier needs no payment method; AI Studio shows your current usage and limits.

onboarding.preset.zhipu.step3: The free model GLM-4.7-Flash works without adding credit.

onboarding.preset.deepseek.cost: You pay for what you use. Correcting and translating a lecture of about one hour costs roughly 1–2 yuan. It costs less at night (Beijing time).

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.intro: LectureFlow is a program that runs on your own computer. This page explains what it keeps, and what it sends where and when.
privacy.local.title: What stays on this computer
privacy.local.1: Your recordings, videos, syllabi and slides are kept in LectureFlow's data folder.
privacy.local.2: Speech recognition, text extraction, playback and subtitles all happen on this computer. Recordings are not sent to any model service. (For the exception when Google Colab remote transcription is on, see below.)
privacy.local.3: Transcripts, translations, glossaries and your edits are kept in a database on this computer.
privacy.sent.title: What is sent to model services
privacy.sent.1: LectureFlow only contacts a model service (such as DeepSeek) after you have set it up.
privacy.sent.2: It sends the text needed for correction and translation: the transcribed sentences, relevant text from the syllabus and slides, the glossary and lecture titles. The recording itself is never sent.
privacy.sent.3: You can see and change which service does what under “Roles” in Settings. The provider's own privacy policy applies to the text it receives.
privacy.sent.4: Some free services' terms allow the provider to use what you send to improve its models. If that matters to you, choose a paid service or the “Transcription only” plan.
privacy.keys.title: API keys
privacy.keys.1: API keys are stored only in the database on this computer and are only used for requests to their provider.
privacy.keys.2: The interface only shows the first and last few characters of a key; exported diagnostics never contain keys.
privacy.downloads.title: Component downloads and updates
privacy.downloads.1: On first use, LectureFlow downloads the runtime and models from the source you chose (default or a mirror) and verifies every file.
privacy.downloads.2: Checking for updates only fetches the version list; none of your data is sent.
privacy.colab.title: Google Colab remote transcription
privacy.colab.1: Recordings are uploaded only if you turn on Google Colab remote transcription. They go to your own Colab session to be transcribed, and the results are downloaded back to this computer.
privacy.none.title: What is not collected
privacy.none.1: LectureFlow collects no usage data, uploads no crash reports, and has no accounts or cloud sync.
privacy.none.2: “Export diagnostics” creates a file only when you select it, and you decide whether to share it. It never contains lecture content or API keys.
privacy.none.3: LectureFlow serves its interface only on this computer's loopback address; other devices on your network cannot reach it.
privacy.delete.title: Deleting
privacy.delete.1: Deleting a lecture or a course also deletes its recordings and results.
privacy.delete.2: After uninstalling LectureFlow, delete its data folder to remove everything.
privacy.footer: LectureFlow is open-source software (AGPL-3.0-or-later); everything described here can be checked in its source code.
